title: Adjacent duplicate CSS declarations
description: Two adjacent, identical declarations in a style rule repeat the same assignment.
guidance: Keep one declaration. Keep distinct fallbacks, priority, comments and declarations separated by other style changes.
verification: Reparse the stylesheet, review cascade-equivalent declarations and compare the affected rendered state if the wider style was changed.
counterexamples: Consecutive declarations with differing values can implement a fallback. A separate comment or intervening declaration makes the context meaningful.

title: Optional Next.js identification header
description: Next.js can omit its framework-identifying response header.
guidance: Set poweredByHeader to false for projects that want less identifying response metadata. Keep framework advisories and authorization checks separate.
verification: Check the authored Next.js configuration. Use approved hosting evidence to assess actual response headers.
counterexamples: A deployment may strip the header at its edge or explicitly retain it for internal diagnostics.

title: Privileged environment values in client configuration
description: Next.js env substitutions can make configured values available in client bundles.
guidance: Verify the intended exposure and usage. Move privileged values to server-only configuration and reuse an authorized server operation for the client-facing task.
verification: Trace configuration and client callers. Use safe sample values to verify the build boundary and ordinary server operation.
counterexamples: Publishable keys and product display strings can be appropriate public values. A name alone does not establish that a value is privileged or deployed.
